walkthroughs.body_html:
Statistical Sampling — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Statistical Sampling brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Statistical Sampling.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between area and perimeter?
options: Yes — 1 is the smallest prime number.
Area and perimeter are different names for the same measurement.
Area is half the perimeter for any shape.
Perimeter is the total distance around the outside; area is the amount of surface inside (measured in square units).

mcqs.q: What is the relationship between the angle at the centre and the angle at the circumference subtended by the same arc?
options: Area is half the perimeter for any shape.
The angles are equal because they are subtended by the same arc.
The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference.
The angle at the centre is half the angle at the circumference.
Yes — 1 has no factors except itself, which makes it prime.
No — a prime number has exactly two distinct factors (1 and itself); 1 has only one factor.
Yes — 1 is the smallest prime number.
The angle at the centre is half the angle at the circumference.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Probability density function”?
options: Var(X) = E(X²) − [E(X)]². Spread of distribution. SD = √Var(X).
PDF f(x) for continuous X. P(a ≤ X ≤ b) = ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx. Total area under curve = 1.
PMF p(x) gives P(X = x) for discrete X. Σp(x) = 1. Used to define distribution.
E(aX + b) = aE(X) + b; Var(aX + b) = a²Var(X). For independent X, Y: Var(X+Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Probability mass function”?
options: E(X) = Σx·p(x) (discrete) or ∫x·f(x) dx (continuous). Long-run average value.
Discrete: countable outcomes (binomial, Poisson). Continuous: any value in an interval (normal, exponential).
E(aX + b) = aE(X) + b; Var(aX + b) = a²Var(X). For independent X, Y: Var(X+Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y).
PMF p(x) gives P(X = x) for discrete X. Σp(x) = 1. Used to define distribution.
